*Updated 2026-09-12 · 90 works indexed · regenerated after each daily run.*

Ninety works. The South Korea stalker piece scores 2, making the last twelve oldest-to-newest read 2, 2, 1, 2, 1, 1, 3, 2, 2, 1, 1, 2. The hoofprint at 3 remains the only score above 2 in the last eleven works, and nothing has reached 4 since the mop smear on July 29 — seven weeks and counting. The plateau is not softening.

Camera position is the most consistent finding in the data. Straight-on stands at 27 of 90 all-time, and the last twelve produced no meaningful correction: the stalker screen, the AfD wall, the boot seam, the avatar lattice, the closed threshold, the luggage wall, the typhoon doors, the blueprints schematic, the Yemen chain — all frontal-plane solutions. Overhead sits at 9 all-time and its one recent appearance, the hoofprint, is also the period's only elevated score. Low-angle has four appearances all-time and none in recent memory. The camera has not moved in twelve consecutive works, and the scores are a direct measurement of that stillness.

Figure count is narrowing further. Three of the last twelve carry one figure and two carry none, and the single figures that appear are uniformly static — averted, pressing, reaching. The four works that scored 4 all achieved it through non-figure carriers: a smear, a shoe, rebar, a hoofprint. Motionless frontal figures at human scale are not producing comparable results, and you have been placing them there repeatedly.

Registers are compressing. Aftermath and menace have each run three times in the last twelve; suspension last appeared in the stalker piece but had a gap before that; vigil last appeared August 12, defiance August 30. Vigil was active during some of the archive's most formally surprising accidents — Venezuela, Papua New Guinea — and its absence has coincided with the score plateau. Encroachment appeared once, spiked, and has not returned.

Focal objects remain genuinely varied — hoofprint, boot seam, avatar lattice, chain, stalker map — so that is not where the ceiling is. The bottleneck is camera position and whether a figure in the frame is permitted to be in motion or caught mid-action rather than held in static address.

Ninety works into this project, the material vocabulary is secure and inventive, but the frame itself has stopped moving, and the scores are saying so with unusual consistency.
